I ruled No, with moderate confidence. Option 0 (Refuse) doesn't apply: the rules can be applied as written, and no immoral-activity exception covers the parties. Option 3 (50/50) doesn't apply because the rules contain no 50-50 clause. Option 4 (Too early) doesn't apply either. Under the rules, a Yes needs a Russian air or missile strike aimed at any location in Kyiv city on 17 October 2026, Kyiv time. That window runs from 16 Oct 21:00 UTC to 17 Oct 21:00 UTC. The market ended on 18 Oct at 03:59 UTC. Even the three-day window for conflicting reports closed around 20 Oct at 21:00 UTC, before the disputes at 21:51 UTC on 20 Oct and 00:00 UTC on 21 Oct. So the market could be resolved when the dispute was filed. I used only reporting dated before 21 Oct 2026, the cutoff the case sets. I did not consult Polymarket, UMA or any report of how this market settled.

The evidence: on the night into 17 October, Russia launched a large strike starting at 18:00 on 16 October. Ukraine's Air Force put it at 332 Shahed-type drones (31 of them jet-powered), Iskander-M/KN-23 ballistic missiles, Kh-22/32 missiles and four Kalibr missiles, with hits at 22 locations. The Kyiv Independent's round-up of that attack (published 17 Oct, updated 12:48) lists casualties and damage region by region. It covers Kharkiv, Sumy, Dnipropetrovsk, Vinnytsia, Odesa, Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson oblasts, but not Kyiv city. Al Jazeera's 17 October report names strikes on Kharkiv, Kramatorsk, Volyn and Rivne, also with no Kyiv strike. UA.News's write-up of the Air Force report doesn't mention Kyiv. The Ukrainian Women's Guard daily summary for 17 October covers Kyiv only with earlier events: the 10–15 October strikes, air-raid statistics, and evening power cuts in Kyiv oblast on 16 October. Coverage of Kyiv on 17 October is about a protest on Khreshchatyk calling for Mayor Klitschko to resign, not an attack. The next strikes clearly aimed at Kyiv came on the night of 18–19 October. AP/ABC, the Kyiv Post and ISW all report Iskander and other ballistic missiles plus drones hitting Kyiv then, after a large daytime drone wave on 18 October. That falls outside the market date. A tweet on that attack is dated 18 October, which is most likely US time, while every report places the attack early on 19 October, Kyiv time.

Across the reports I found, there is no confirmed strike on Kyiv city on 17 October. Burden: Yes needs an affirmative qualifying action, and none appeared in the sources I could check. The main risk is that I couldn't fully check the evening of 17 October (see gaps), so this is my best-supported ruling rather than a certain one.

The market-specific Primary Document and its definition of “target Kyiv” are absent, leaving the decisive resolution criterion unknown. The record also contains no evidence establishing or refuting any qualifying Russian action in Kyiv on October 17, 2026. Because the date and deadline passed, “Too early” is unsupported, while “50/50” cannot substitute for missing proof; the essential defect in the record therefore warrants refusal to arbitrate.

# Dispute 318, round 0: "Will Russia target Kyiv on October 17, 2026?" (PM-5167158)

## Decision

**Yes (choice 2).** Russia carried out a qualifying military action directed at the city of Kyiv on 17 October 2026, Kyiv time. The disputed "No" proposals were wrong.

## What the rules require

The market resolves "Yes" if Russia targets Kyiv with an air strike or a surface-to-surface missile strike on the specified date, Kyiv time. One-way attack drones (Shahed-type) are expressly a qualifying surface-to-surface strike. Interception does not matter: an action made up mostly or entirely of munitions shot down before impact still qualifies, and where they landed or whether damage resulted "will not be considered". A strike is "directed at Kyiv" if it targets any location within the city. Resolution sources are official Ukrainian and Russian government and military information plus a consensus of credible reporting. No Polymarket clarifications were posted. Evidence cut-off under the court policy is 2026-10-21 00:00 UTC.

## The record

The only evidence item is the case record PDF (CID `QmeBT7H1MBHEyyeV7BZ7MYK1VhnsmSJXnxLEWWBNtrZaFX`), one page. It was rendered to PNG and read with vision; the page image matches the text layer (the OCR binary was missing on the box, so the vision read stood in for OCR). It gives the timeline (market end 18 Oct 03:59 UTC; "No" proposals disputed 20 Oct 21:51 UTC and 21 Oct 00:00 UTC), the Polygon question ID, and notes that neither party filed reasons, so jurors must search themselves. Nothing in it addresses the juror. There is no video or still evidence.

Independent research, all published on 17 October 2026, before the cut-off:

1. **Overnight drone attack on the city (about 04:30-05:00 Kyiv time, 17 Oct).** RBC-Ukraine (04:51, 17 Oct), citing the Ukrainian Air Force's Telegram and the Kyiv City Military Administration: the KMVA declared a red-level alert at 04:33 and urged residents into shelters, and "in parallel Kyiv came under attack by enemy drones; explosions were heard repeatedly in the city." Korol Danylo (09:56) and Znaj.ua (06:50) report the same, the former saying explosions were heard "in various districts of the capital".
2. **The wider barrage it was part of.** The Air Force counted, for the night of 16-17 October, Iskander-M/KN-23 ballistic missiles, Kh-22/32 and four Kalibr cruise missiles, and 332 Shahed-type drones; 293 targets were downed or suppressed and hits recorded at 22 locations (Ukrainska Pravda, Kyiv Post, Fakty ICTV, Kyiv Independent).
3. **Evening of 17 Oct (Kyiv time).** NV's live feed relays Air Force alerts at 21:25 ("jet Shaheds flying at Kyiv from the south") and 21:30 ("a jet Shahed toward Kyiv ... jet Shaheds heading toward Poltava and the Obolon district of Kyiv"), with the capital's air-raid alert still running. UNN (19:50, 17 Oct), citing the Air Force's daytime tally of 157 drones and six S-8000 missiles, reports "explosions were heard in Kyiv".

I found no Russian denial or conflicting official account. One search result that looked relevant (a Klitschko Telegram post on debris in Darnytskyi, Holosiivskyi and Pechersk districts) turned out on checking to be dated February 2026 and was **not** relied on. A 34.ua piece describing the 17 Oct attack on Kyiv reads as generic and was also not relied on.

## Why this is material

The rules ask only whether Russia launched a qualifying strike at a location in Kyiv city on 17 October, Kyiv time. Shahed-type one-way attack drones are named as qualifying, and interception and absence of damage are expressly irrelevant. Ukrainian official sources (the Air Force and the KMVA alert) and several independent outlets agree that Kyiv city was attacked by drones in the early hours of 17 October, and the Air Force tracked further jet-powered Shaheds heading at Kyiv, including its Obolon district, that evening. Either episode alone satisfies the rule. Because sources agree on occurrence, attribution, timing and target, the three-day "conflicting reports" extension does not come into play, and the market was resolvable when the proposals were made, so "Too early" does not fit. Nothing calls for 50/50 or Invalid.

## Conclusion

On the record available before 21 Oct 00:00 UTC, Russia targeted Kyiv with one-way attack drones on 17 October 2026 (Kyiv time). The market should resolve **Yes**. Vote: choice 2.
